title: Image Metadata Inspector
metaDescription: Inspect drone and aerial photos for embedded GPS coordinates, camera data, and other identifying metadata.
description: Inspect drone and aerial photos for embedded GPS coordinates, camera data, and other identifying metadata.

educational.howItWorks: This tool reads the metadata stored inside an image file. In JPEG, PNG, WebP and TIFF files it walks the whole Exif structure (IFD0, the Exif, GPS and Interop directories, and IFD1 with the embedded thumbnail) and lists each tag by name, or by number when the tag is not a standard one. It also decodes the common XMP and IPTC fields, PNG text chunks and JPEG and GIF comments. Maker notes are listed by size but not decoded, and HEIC and AVIF photos are recognised but not read; so is a BigTIFF, which can carry the same Exif as a JPEG. When a block is found that it cannot decode, or a cap or a broken file stops the read, the result says so instead of reporting the photo as clean.
tips: Always strip metadata from photos before sharing online, especially GPS coordinates
Phones add precise GPS coordinates to every photo while camera location is on — check your settings
Screenshots typically contain less metadata than camera photos
Use the clean copy: it redraws only the pixels into a new JPEG, so no Exif, XMP or IPTC block is carried over
Check metadata in photos before posting on dating apps or social media
commonMistakes: Assuming social media platforms strip all metadata — many preserve some data in their backend
Not disabling location services for your camera app, embedding GPS in every photo
Sharing original photos via email or messaging without stripping metadata first
Forgetting that camera model and software information can identify you
Not checking photos received from others for metadata before re-sharing
